claim: Generation of oligodendrocytes in the adult brain enables both adaptive changes in neural circuits and regeneration of myelin sheaths destroyed by injury, disease, and normal aging.
source: Generation of oligodendrocytes in the adult brain enables both adaptive changes in neural circuits and regeneration of myelin sheaths destroyed by injury, disease, and normal aging.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that references established scientific understanding about oligodendrocyte function in the adult brain.

claim: Transformation of oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) into myelinating oligodendrocytes requires processing of distinct mRNAs at different stages of cell maturation.
source: This transformation of oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) into myelinating oligodendrocytes requires processing of distinct mRNAs at different stages of cell maturation.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge about the biological process of oligodendrocyte maturation.

claim: Mislocalization and aggregation of the RNA-binding protein, TDP-43, occur in both neurons and glia in neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Although mislocalization and aggregation of the RNA-binding protein, TDP-43, occur in both neurons and glia in neurodegenerative diseases, the consequences of TDP-43 loss within different stages of the oligodendrocyte lineage are not well understood.
evidence: This statement references established observations in the field of neurodegenerative disease research.

claim: OPCs depend on TDP-43 for survival, with conditional deletion resulting in cascading cell loss followed by rapid regeneration to restore their density.
source: While OPCs depend on TDP-43 for survival, with conditional deletion resulting in cascading cell loss followed by rapid regeneration to restore their density, oligodendrocytes become less sensitive to TDP-43 depletion as they mature.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the Pdgfra-CreER deletion experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: Oligodendrocytes become less sensitive to TDP-43 depletion as they mature.
source: While OPCs depend on TDP-43 for survival, with conditional deletion resulting in cascading cell loss followed by rapid regeneration to restore their density, oligodendrocytes become less sensitive to TDP-43 depletion as they mature.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparing outcomes between Mobp-iCre and MogiCre deletion experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Deletion of TDP-43 early in the oligodendrocyte maturation process led to eventual oligodendrocyte degeneration, seizures, and premature lethality.
source: Deletion of TDP-43 early in the maturation process led to eventual oligodendrocyte degeneration, seizures, and premature lethality, while oligodendrocytes that experienced late deletion survived and mice exhibited a normal lifespan.
evidence: This is supported by data from Mobp-TDP43 KO mice shown in Figure 2B and related experiments.

claim: Oligodendrocytes that experienced late deletion of TDP-43 survived and mice exhibited a normal lifespan.
source: Deletion of TDP-43 early in the maturation process led to eventual oligodendrocyte degeneration, seizures, and premature lethality, while oligodendrocytes that experienced late deletion survived and mice exhibited a normal lifespan.
evidence: This is supported by data from Mog-TDP43 KO mice shown in Figure 2B.

claim: TDP-43-deficient oligodendrocytes formed fewer and thinner myelin sheaths at both early and late deletion stages.
source: At both stages, TDP-43-deficient oligodendrocytes formed fewer and thinner myelin sheaths and extended new processes that inappropriately wrapped neuronal somata and blood vessels.
evidence: This is supported by transmission electron microscopy data shown in Figure 3.

claim: TDP-43-deficient oligodendrocytes extended new processes that inappropriately wrapped neuronal somata and blood vessels.
source: At both stages, TDP-43-deficient oligodendrocytes formed fewer and thinner myelin sheaths and extended new processes that inappropriately wrapped neuronal somata and blood vessels.
evidence: This is supported by immunohistochemistry and in vivo imaging data shown in Figure 4.

claim: In the absence of TDP-43, key proteins involved in oligodendrocyte maturation and myelination were misspliced, leading to aberrant incorporation of cryptic exons.
source: Transcriptional analysis revealed that in the absence of TDP-43, key proteins involved in oligodendrocyte maturation and myelination were misspliced, leading to aberrant incorporation of cryptic exons.
evidence: This is supported by RNA-Seq data and RT-PCR validation shown in Figure 6.

claim: Inducible deletion of TDP-43 from oligodendrocytes in the adult CNS induced progressive morphological changes and mice acquired profound hindlimb weakness.
source: Inducible deletion of TDP-43 from oligodendrocytes in the adult central nervous system (CNS) induced the same progressive morphological changes and mice acquired profound hindlimb weakness, suggesting that loss of TDP-43 function in oligodendrocytes may contribute to neuronal dysfunction in neurodegenerative disease.
evidence: This is supported by data from Mobp-iCreER experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: New oligodendrocytes continue to be generated in response to changes in experience, such as enhanced sensory input and intense motor learning.
source: The distribution of myelin in the adult brain is not static, as new oligodendrocytes continue to be generated in response to changes in experience, such as enhanced sensory input and intense motor learning (Hughes et al., 2018; Xiao et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Oligodendrocyte lineage cells exist in a developmental continuum throughout life, consisting of OPCs that maintain their density through proliferation and cells in the process of maturing from premyelinating to myelinating oligodendrocytes.
source: As a result, oligodendrocyte lineage cells exist in a developmental continuum throughout life, consisting of oligodendrocyte precursor cells (OPCs) that maintain their density through proliferation (Hughes et al., 2013), and cells in the process of maturing from premyelinating to myelinating oligodendrocytes.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research on OPC proliferation.

claim: Ongoing oligodendrogenesis is necessary to prolong the period of circuit maturation.
source: This ongoing oligodendrogenesis is necessary to prolong the period of circuit maturation (Benamer et al., 2020), enable adaptive changes in myelination (Gibson et al., 2014), and restore myelin lost through aging or demyelinating injuries (Orthmann-Murphy et al., 2020; Bacmeister et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Ongoing oligodendrogenesis enables adaptive changes in myelination.
source: This ongoing oligodendrogenesis is necessary to prolong the period of circuit maturation (Benamer et al., 2020), enable adaptive changes in myelination (Gibson et al., 2014), and restore myelin lost through aging or demyelinating injuries (Orthmann-Murphy et al., 2020; Bacmeister et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Ongoing oligodendrogenesis restores myelin lost through aging or demyelinating injuries.
source: This ongoing oligodendrogenesis is necessary to prolong the period of circuit maturation (Benamer et al., 2020), enable adaptive changes in myelination (Gibson et al., 2014), and restore myelin lost through aging or demyelinating injuries (Orthmann-Murphy et al., 2020; Bacmeister et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The transition from progenitor to myelin-forming oligodendrocyte requires profound transcriptional changes, in which myelin-associated gene networks are activated and mRNAs are transported to distal processes.
source: The transition from progenitor to myelin-forming oligodendrocyte requires profound transcriptional changes, in which myelin-associated gene networks are activated and mRNAs are transported to distal processes to direct sites of axon ensheathment and membrane compaction (Müller et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: TDP-43 is a DNA/RNA-binding protein that serves as a master regulator of RNA metabolism, controlling transcriptional integrity, post-transcriptional stability, and localization of mRNAs.
source: TDP-43 (TAR DNA-binding protein 43 kDa) is a DNA/RNA-binding protein that serves as a master regulator of RNA metabolism, controlling transcriptional integrity, post-transcriptional stability, and localization of mRNAs (Warraich et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Within the nucleus, TDP-43 prevents incorporation of cryptic exons into mature mRNA by binding to UG-rich motifs within intronic sequences.
source: Within the nucleus, TDP-43 prevents incorporation of cryptic exons into mature mRNA by binding to UG-rich motifs within intronic sequences (Ling et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Loss of TDP-43 in neurons results in missplicing of pre-mRNAs, resulting in gain and loss of function alterations in the landscape of expressed proteins.
source: Loss of TDP-43 in neurons results in missplicing of pre-mRNAs, resulting in gain and loss of function alterations in the landscape of expressed proteins that influence their structure, function, and longevity (Ling et al., 2015; Donde et al., 2019; Ma et al., 2021; Brown et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Cytoplasmic mislocalization and aberrant aggregation of TDP-43 have been observed in affected regions of the CNS in frontotemporal dementia, Alzheimer's disease, amyotropic lateral sclerosis, and multiple sclerosis.
source: In many neurodegenerative diseases, including frontotemporal dementia, Alzheimer's disease (AD), amyotropic lateral sclerosis (ALS), and multiple sclerosis (MS), cytoplasmic mislocalization and aberrant aggregation of TDP-43 have been observed in affected regions of the CNS (Neumann et al., 2006; Ling et al., 2015; Sun et al., 2017; Masaki et al., 2020; Salapa et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Mutations in TARDBP are responsible for both familial and sporadic forms of ALS.
source: Moreover, mutations in TARDBP are responsible for both familial and sporadic forms of ALS (Kapeli et al., 2017; Ince et al., 2011), suggesting that altered mRNA processing by TDP-43 may contribute to cellular pathology and functional impairment in both sporadic and inherited forms of neurodegenerative disease.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Nuclear exclusion and cytoplasmic aggregation of TDP-43 occur in glial cells in MS.
source: Although neurons have been the primary focus of research into TDP-43-associated pathologies, nuclear exclusion, and cytoplasmic aggregation of TDP-43 also occur in glial cells in neurodegenerative diseases, such as MS (Neumann et al., 2006; Masaki et al., 2020; Rohan et al., 2014), suggesting that glial cell dysfunction could impair both OPC homeostasis and remyelination.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Genetic deletion of TDP-43 in mice results in embryonic lethality due to impaired expansion of inner cell mass during early embryogenesis.
source: Genetic deletion of TDP-43 in mice results in embryonic lethality due to impaired expansion of inner cell mass during early embryogenesis (Sephton et al., 2010), suggesting that it is essential for cell survival.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Selective deletion experiments indicate that the effects of TDP-43 are cell type specific and diverse.
source: However, selective deletion experiments indicate that the effects of TDP-43 are cell type specific and diverse (Jeong et al., 2017), reflecting differences in transcriptional state.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Conditional inactivation of TDP-43 in neurons induces impairment in neuronal function and progressive neurodegeneration.
source: In neurons, conditional inactivation of TDP-43 induces impairment in neuronal function and progressive neurodegeneration (Donde et al., 2019; Iguchi et al., 2013; Yang et al., 2014; Wu et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Conditional knockout of Tardbp in microglia enhanced expression of NF-κB and NLRP3, leading to a more activated phenotype characterized by enhanced phagocytosis.
source: Conditional knockout of Tardbp in microglia enhanced expression of NF-κB and NLRP3, leading to a more activated phenotype characterized by enhanced phagocytosis (Zhao et al., 2015; Paolicelli et al., 2017), while loss of TDP-43 in astrocytes promoted their transition to a reactive A1 phenotype associated with neuronal injury (Peng et al., 2020; Walker et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Loss of TDP-43 in astrocytes promoted their transition to a reactive A1 phenotype associated with neuronal injury.
source: Conditional knockout of Tardbp in microglia enhanced expression of NF-κB and NLRP3, leading to a more activated phenotype characterized by enhanced phagocytosis (Zhao et al., 2015; Paolicelli et al., 2017), while loss of TDP-43 in astrocytes promoted their transition to a reactive A1 phenotype associated with neuronal injury (Peng et al., 2020; Walker et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Genetic deletion of Tardbp in Schwann cells did not affect their survival or myelinic potential, but impaired formation and maintenance of paranodal junctions.
source: In Schwann cells, genetic deletion of Tardbp did not affect their survival or myelinic potential, but impaired formation and maintenance of paranodal junctions (Chang et al., 2021), while deletion from both newly generated oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells induced necroptosis of oligodendrocytes and early mortality (Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Deletion of Tardbp from both newly generated oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells induced necroptosis of oligodendrocytes and early mortality.
source: In Schwann cells, genetic deletion of Tardbp did not affect their survival or myelinic potential, but impaired formation and maintenance of paranodal junctions (Chang et al., 2021), while deletion from both newly generated oligodendrocytes and Schwann cells induced necroptosis of oligodendrocytes and early mortality (Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Pdgfra-CreER;Tardbpfl/fl;RCE mice showed 94.75% recombination efficiency in OPCs at P90+14.
source: Immunolabeling for EGFP and NG2, a proteoglycan highly expressed by OPCs, revealed that this manipulation induced recombination in most OPCs (EGFP+NG2+/NG2+ cells: 94.75 ± 0.75%, n = 4) (Figure 1B), resulting in near complete depletion of OPCs from the corpus callosum, while those in the overlying cortical gray matter were preserved (Figure 1C,E; Figure 1D, panel i) (OPCs/mm3: Corpus callosum 14 dpi, Control = 6910 ± 201; cKO = 987 ± 201, n = 3, p < 0.001, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple comparisons test).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data.

claim: OPC density in the corpus callosum at 14 dpi was 6910 ± 201 cells/mm³ in controls and 987 ± 201 cells/mm³ in PDGFRα-TDP43 cKO mice.
source: Immunolabeling for EGFP and NG2, a proteoglycan highly expressed by OPCs, revealed that this manipulation induced recombination in most OPCs (EGFP+NG2+/NG2+ cells: 94.75 ± 0.75%, n = 4) (Figure 1B), resulting in near complete depletion of OPCs from the corpus callosum, while those in the overlying cortical gray matter were preserved (Figure 1C,E; Figure 1D, panel i) (OPCs/mm3: Corpus callosum 14 dpi, Control = 6910 ± 201; cKO = 987 ± 201, n = 3, p < 0.001, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple comparisons test).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: OPCs in cortical gray matter were depleted at P90+30 in PDGFRα-TDP43 cKO mice.
source: However, when the interval between tamoxifen administration and sacrifice was increased to 30 days (P90 + 30), OPCs in gray matter were also depleted (Figure 1C,E; Figure 1D, panel ii) (OPCs/mm3: Cortex 30 dpi, Control = 5247 ± 236; cKO = 811 ± 187, n = 3, p < 0.001, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple comparisons test).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: OPC density in the cortex at 30 dpi was 5247 ± 236 cells/mm³ in controls and 811 ± 187 cells/mm³ in PDGFRα-TDP43 cKO mice.
source: However, when the interval between tamoxifen administration and sacrifice was increased to 30 days (P90 + 30), OPCs in gray matter were also depleted (Figure 1C,E; Figure 1D, panel ii) (OPCs/mm3: Cortex 30 dpi, Control = 5247 ± 236; cKO = 811 ± 187, n = 3, p < 0.001, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple comparisons test).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: OPCs in white matter had repopulated by P90+30 in PDGFRα-TDP43 cKO mice.
source: Remarkably, OPCs in white matter had repopulated by this time, and highly polarized OPCs were visible migrating out of the corpus callosum into the gray matter (Figure 1C, red arrowhead; Figure 1D, panel iii; Figure 1E).
evidence: This observation is supported by microscopy images shown in Figure 1.

claim: OPCs regained their normal density and tiled distribution throughout gray and white matter by P90+60 in PDGFRα-TDP43 cKO mice.
source: When the interval between tamoxifen administration and sacrifice was increased by another 30 days (P90 + 60), OPCs had regained their normal density and tiled distribution throughout gray and white matter (Figure 1C,E).
evidence: This observation is supported by microscopy images and quantification shown in Figure 1.

claim: Repopulation of OPCs was associated with enhanced proliferation, visible by increased Ki-67 immunoreactivity in PDGFRα-TDP43 cKO.
source: As expected, this repopulation was associated with enhanced proliferation of OPCs, visible by increased Ki-67 immunoreactivity in PDGFRα-TDP43 cKO (Figure 1F; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This observation is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: There were no signs of astrogliosis after extensive death of OPCs, as assessed by GFAP immunoreactivity.
source: Despite this extensive death of OPCs, there were no signs of astrogliosis, as assessed by glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) immunoreactivity (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B), in accordance with the tolerance to normal turnover of these cells (Hughes et al., 2013).
evidence: This observation is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and a citation to previous research.

claim: Deletion of Tardbp in P180 mice resulted in robust loss of OPCs in the corpus callosum within 14 days.
source: Deletion of Tardbp in P180 mice also resulted in a robust loss of OPCs in the corpus callosum within 14 days (P180 + 14) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C), indicating that the dependence on TDP-43 extends into the adult CNS.
evidence: This observation is supported by microscopy images shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Mobp expression is robust at the premyelinating oligodendrocyte stage, whereas expression of Mog does not increase substantially until the myelin-forming stage.
source: Single-cell RNA-Seq results indicate that Mobp expression is robust at the premyelinating oligodendrocyte stage, whereas expression of Mog does not increase substantially until the myelin-forming stage (Marques et al., 2016; Hrvatin et al., 2018; Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous single-cell RNA-Seq studies and data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: Mobp-TDP43 KO mice began to exhibit spontaneous seizures at approximately P110.
source: Mice in which TDP-43 was constitutively removed from premyelinating oligodendrocytes (Mobp-iCre;Tardbpfl/fl;RCE) (Mobp-TDP43 KO) began to exhibit spontaneous seizures at ~P110 (Figure 2B, red arrowhead; Video 1) and 100% died prematurely by P180 (Figure 2B, dark orange line), similar to the phenotype exhibited by CnpCre;Tardbpfl/fl mice (Wang et al., 2018), in which recombination occurs in OPCs, early postmitotic oligodendrocytes, and Schwann cells in the PNS (Lappe-Siefke et al., 2003; Chang et al., 2021; Tognatta et al., 2017).
evidence: This observation is supported by survival curve data shown in Figure 2B and video documentation.

claim: 100% of Mobp-TDP43 KO mice died prematurely by P180.
source: Mice in which TDP-43 was constitutively removed from premyelinating oligodendrocytes (Mobp-iCre;Tardbpfl/fl;RCE) (Mobp-TDP43 KO) began to exhibit spontaneous seizures at ~P110 (Figure 2B, red arrowhead; Video 1) and 100% died prematurely by P180 (Figure 2B, dark orange line), similar to the phenotype exhibited by CnpCre;Tardbpfl/fl mice (Wang et al., 2018), in which recombination occurs in OPCs, early postmitotic oligodendrocytes, and Schwann cells in the PNS (Lappe-Siefke et al., 2003; Chang et al., 2021; Tognatta et al., 2017).
evidence: This observation is supported by survival curve data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Mog-TDP43 KO mice did not exhibit spontaneous seizures or other gross behavioral abnormalities and survived as well as controls.
source: In contrast, mice in which TDP-43 was deleted from mature oligodendrocytes (MogiCre;Tardbpfl/fl;RCE) (Mog-TDP43 KO) did not exhibit spontaneous seizures or other gross behavioral abnormalities and survived as well as controls (Figure 2B, blue lines).
evidence: This observation is supported by survival curve data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: There was no change in the density of ASPA+ mature oligodendrocytes in the motor cortex of Mobp-TDP43 KO or Mog-TDP43 KO mice at P30, P90, or P180.
source: In contrast to the extensive demyelination and oligodendrocyte necroptosis observed in CnpCre;Tardbpfl/fl mice (Wang et al., 2018), there was no change in the density of ASPA+ mature oligodendrocytes in the motor cortex of Mobp-TDP43 KO or Mog-TDP43 KO mice at P30, P90, or P180 (end stage) (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This observation is supported by immunohistochemistry and quantification data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: Early deletion of TDP-43 in premyelinating oligodendrocytes (Mobp-TDP43 KO) was associated with a dramatic increase in Ki-67+ OPCs at P90.
source: Early deletion of TDP-43 in premyelinating oligodendrocytes (Mobp-TDP43 KO) was associated with a dramatic increase in Ki-67+ OPCs at P90 (Figure 2E,F) (Ki-67+ OPCs/mm3: Mobp-TDP43 Control = 71 ± 45; Mobp-TDP43 KO = 941 ± 121, n = 4, p < 0.001, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple comparisons test), whereas deletion of TDP-43 from mature oligodendrocytes (Mog-TDP43 KO) was not associated with a significant change in OPC proliferation (Figure 2E,F) (Ki-67+ OPCs: Mog-TDP43 Control = 24 ± 24; Mog-TDP43 KO = 212 ± 89, n = 4, p > 0.05, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple comparisons test).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: Ki-67+ OPC density at P90 was 71 ± 45 cells/mm³ in Mobp-TDP43 Control and 941 ± 121 cells/mm³ in Mobp-TDP43 KO.
source: Early deletion of TDP-43 in premyelinating oligodendrocytes (Mobp-TDP43 KO) was associated with a dramatic increase in Ki-67+ OPCs at P90 (Figure 2E,F) (Ki-67+ OPCs/mm3: Mobp-TDP43 Control = 71 ± 45; Mobp-TDP43 KO = 941 ± 121, n = 4, p < 0.001, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple comparisons test), whereas deletion of TDP-43 from mature oligodendrocytes (Mog-TDP43 KO) was not associated with a significant change in OPC proliferation (Figure 2E,F) (Ki-67+ OPCs: Mog-TDP43 Control = 24 ± 24; Mog-TDP43 KO = 212 ± 89, n = 4, p > 0.05, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple comparisons test).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: Deletion of TDP-43 from mature oligodendrocytes (Mog-TDP43 KO) was not associated with a significant change in OPC proliferation.
source: Early deletion of TDP-43 in premyelinating oligodendrocytes (Mobp-TDP43 KO) was associated with a dramatic increase in Ki-67+ OPCs at P90 (Figure 2E,F) (Ki-67+ OPCs/mm3: Mobp-TDP43 Control = 71 ± 45; Mobp-TDP43 KO = 941 ± 121, n = 4, p < 0.001, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple comparisons test), whereas deletion of TDP-43 from mature oligodendrocytes (Mog-TDP43 KO) was not associated with a significant change in OPC proliferation (Figure 2E,F) (Ki-67+ OPCs: Mog-TDP43 Control = 24 ± 24; Mog-TDP43 KO = 212 ± 89, n = 4, p > 0.05, one-way ANOVA with Tukey's multiple comparisons test).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data with statistical analysis.

claim: There was an increase in the number of newly formed oligodendrocytes in Mobp-TDP43 KO, as assessed by lncOL1 expression.
source: Moreover, there was an increase in the number of newly formed oligodendrocytes in Mobp-TDP43 KO, as assessed by the emergence of cells that expressed lncOL1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A), a long noncoding RNA that is transiently expressed in premyelinating oligodendrocytes (He et al., 2017), suggesting that there is an increased turnover of oligodendrocytes.
evidence: This observation is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4A and a citation to previous research.

claim: Astrogliosis was prominent in Mobp-TDP43 KO mice.
source: Astrogliosis (visible through the increase in GFAP immunoreactivity) was also prominent in Mobp-TDP43 KO mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B, C), further supporting the conclusion that early deletion of TDP-43 leads to degeneration and subsequent regeneration of oligodendrocytes.
evidence: This observation is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 4B, C.

claim: Myelinated axons in Mobp-TDP43 KO and Mog-TDP43 KO mice had significantly higher G ratios than controls at both P90 and P180.
source: Myelinated axons in Mobp-TDP43 KO and Mog-TDP43 KO mice had significantly higher G ratios than controls at both P90 and P180, with thinner sheaths formed (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: This observation is supported by transmission electron microscopy data and G ratio analysis shown in Figure 3A–D.

claim: The number of myelinated axons was reduced in both Mobp-TDP43 KO and Mog-TDP43 KO mice.
source: In addition to thinner myelin sheaths, the number of myelinated axons was also reduced in both oligodendrocyte TDP-43 knockouts (Figure 3E,F).
evidence: This observation is supported by transmission electron microscopy data and quantification shown in Figure 3E,F.

claim: Mog-TDP43 KO oligodendrocytes tended to exhibit less MBP immunoreactivity per process.
source: Morphological reconstructions of individual oligodendrocytes and their associated myelin sheaths revealed that Mog-TDP43 KO oligodendrocytes tended to exhibit less myelin basic protein (MBP) immunoreactivity per process (revealed by EGFP labeling), indicative of decreased myelin production (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This observation is supported by morphological reconstruction data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: TDP-43-null oligodendrocytes frequently exhibited abnormal nodes of Ranvier.
source: Immunocytochemical analysis revealed that TDP-43-null oligodendrocytes also frequently exhibited abnormal nodes of Ranvier (NOR). While normal NOR exhibit focal localization of βIV spectrin at the node flanked by Caspr within the paranodes (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A, yellow arrowheads), in mice with TDP-43 KO oligodendrocytes, nodes often consisted of Caspr triads and βIV-spectrin doublets (Figure 3—figure supplement 5A, red arrowheads).
evidence: This observation is supported by immunocytochemistry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 5A.

claim: Some axons exhibited double myelination in TDP-43 KO mice.
source: EM analysis revealed that some axons exhibited double myelination (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), which may contribute to these macroscopic changes in organization of node-associated proteins (Figure 3—figure supplement 5B), as well as unusual accumulation of mitochondria and vacuoles in the inner tongue.
evidence: This observation is supported by electron microscopy data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Oligodendrocyte density gradually increased from P30 to P180 in both control and mutant (KO) mice.
source: Histological analysis of motor cortex in these mice revealed that oligodendrocyte density gradually increased from P30 to P180 in both control and mutant (KO) mice (Figure 2D); however, while EGFP was largely restricted to oligodendrocyte somata in controls, due to the limited cytoplasm in myelin sheaths, mice with TDP-43-deficient oligodendrocytes exhibited a dramatic increase in EGFP fluorescence in the surrounding parenchyma at P90 and P180 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This observation is supported by histological analysis and microscopy data shown in Figure 2D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mice with TDP-43-deficient oligodendrocytes exhibited a dramatic increase in EGFP fluorescence in the surrounding parenchyma at P90 and P180.
source: Histological analysis of motor cortex in these mice revealed that oligodendrocyte density gradually increased from P30 to P180 in both control and mutant (KO) mice (Figure 2D); however, while EGFP was largely restricted to oligodendrocyte somata in controls, due to the limited cytoplasm in myelin sheaths, mice with TDP-43-deficient oligodendrocytes exhibited a dramatic increase in EGFP fluorescence in the surrounding parenchyma at P90 and P180 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This observation is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The morphological change in oligodendrocytes was observed throughout the brain, as well as the optic nerve and spinal cord.
source: This morphological change in oligodendrocytes was observed throughout the brain, as well as the optic nerve and spinal cord (Figure 4—figure supplement 2), suggesting that this phenotype is fully penetrant in the CNS.
evidence: This observation is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: Aberrant structures in TDP-43 KO oligodendrocytes are highly dynamic.
source: Repetitive in vivo two photon imaging of individual oligodendrocytes in the motor cortex of Mobp-TDP43-RCE KO mice over 2 weeks revealed that these aberrant structures are highly dynamic (Figure 4—figure supplement 3; Video 2), indicating that these normally highly stable cells exhibit enhanced growth when TDP-43 is absent.
evidence: This observation is supported by in vivo two-photon imaging data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3 and Video 2.

claim: Much of the additional EGFP fluorescence in TDP-43 KO oligodendrocytes arose from thick cytoplasmic processes that often ended in circular or cuff-like structures.
source: High-resolution imaging revealed that much of this additional EGFP fluorescence arose from thick cytoplasmic processes of oligodendrocytes that often ended in circular or cuff-like structures (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This observation is supported by high-resolution microscopy data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: Circular structures in TDP-43 KO oligodendrocytes arose from inappropriate wrapping of neuronal cell bodies.
source: Immunostaining for NeuN revealed that circular structures arose from inappropriate wrapping of neuronal cell bodies (Figure 4C,D; Video 3).
evidence: This observation is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4C,D and Video 3.

claim: EGFP+ oligodendrocyte processes colocalized with blood vessels labeled with GS-Isolectin.
source: As the cuff-like structures are reminiscent of astrocyte endfeet (Gundersen et al., 2014), we labeled blood vessels with GS-Isolectin, revealing that EGFP+ oligodendrocyte processes also colocalized with these tubular structures (Figure 4E).
evidence: This observation is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4E and a citation to previous research.

claim: In vivo two photon imaging revealed that oligodendrocyte processes extended unbranched processes to ensheath rhodamine-labeled capillaries.
source: To determine if these structures were capillaries, we used in vivo two photon imaging in living Mobp-TDP43-RCE KO mice to visualize both oligodendrocyte processes and capillaries after a retro-orbital injection of dextran–rhodamine. With 4D imaging, it was possible to follow the cytoplasmic processes from individual oligodendrocytes, revealing that they extended unbranched processes to ensheath rhodamine-labeled capillaries (Figure 4F).
evidence: This observation is supported by in vivo two-photon imaging data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Regions of capillaries surrounded by oligodendrocyte cuffs exhibited reduced aquaporin four immunoreactivity.
source: Histological analysis revealed that regions of capillaries surrounded by oligodendrocyte cuffs exhibited reduced aquaporin four immunoreactivity (Figure 4—figure supplement 5A), a protein restricted to astrocyte endfeet (Gundersen et al., 2014), suggesting that these oligodendrocyte wraps may displace or alter the physiology of astrocytes at capillaries.
evidence: This observation is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5A and a citation to previous research.

claim: Some TDP-43 KO oligodendrocytes exhibited immunoreactivity to Ki-67.
source: Remarkably, we also found that some TDP-43 KO oligodendrocytes exhibited immunoreactivity to Ki-67 (Figure 4—figure supplement 5B), suggesting that these cells are reverting to a less mature phenotype.
evidence: This observation is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5B.

claim: ASPA+ oligodendrocytes were present in the motor cortex with morphologies comparable to controls at P90+30 in Mobp-iCreER;Tardbpfl/fl;RCE mice.
source: When tamoxifen was administered to P90 Mobp-iCreER;Tardbpfl/fl;RCE mice and analyzed 30 days later (P90 + 30), ASPA+ oligodendrocytes were present in the motor cortex with morphologies comparable to controls (Mobp-iCreER;Tardbp+/+, fl/+) (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This observation is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5A,B.

claim: The majority of oligodendrocytes exhibited hypertrophy and cytoplasmic ensheathment of neuronal cell bodies and capillaries at P90+90 in TDP-43 mutant mice.
source: However, when TDP-43 mutant mice were analyzed 90 days later (P90 + 90), the majority of oligodendrocytes exhibited hypertrophy, as well as cytoplasmic ensheathment of neuronal cell bodies and capillaries (Figure 5B, yellow arrowhead), indicating that TDP-43 is also required to maintain oligodendrocyte structure in the adult CNS.
evidence: This observation is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Mobp-TDP43 cKO mice exhibited progressive motor problems, including limp tails, hindlimb clasping, and hindlimb weakness, but not seizures or premature lethality.
source: However, the behavioral consequences of TDP-43 deletion in the mature CNS were distinct, as these mice exhibited progressive motor problems, including limp tails, hindlimb clasping (Figure 5C, Video 4), and hindlimb weakness (Figure 5D), but not seizures or premature lethality.
evidence: This observation is supported by behavioral assessment data shown in Figure 5C,D and Video 4.

claim: Mobp-TDP43 cKO mice developed significant motor weakness within 90 days after Cre recombination, as assessed by EAE clinical scoring.
source: We utilized the clinical scoring method established for experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), a mouse model of MS, and found that Mobp-TDP43 cKO developed significant motor weakness within 90 days after Cre recombination (Figure 5E).
evidence: This observation is supported by EAE clinical scoring data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The transformation of oligodendrocytes did not lead to degeneration of motor neurons.
source: Although this transformation of oligodendrocytes did not lead to degeneration of motor neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), the spinal cord exhibited enhanced GFAP immunoreactivity (Figure 5F,G), indicative of widespread inflammation, which has been shown to impair motor function without loss of spinal motor neurons (Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This observation is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1 and Figure 5F,G, and a citation to previous research.

claim: The spinal cord exhibited enhanced GFAP immunoreactivity in Mobp-TDP43 cKO mice.
source: Although this transformation of oligodendrocytes did not lead to degeneration of motor neurons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), the spinal cord exhibited enhanced GFAP immunoreactivity (Figure 5F,G), indicative of widespread inflammation, which has been shown to impair motor function without loss of spinal motor neurons (Wang et al., 2018).
evidence: This observation is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 5F,G.

claim: Hundreds of genes were differentially expressed in both Mobp-TDP43 KO and Mog-TDP43 KO oligodendrocytes, comprising 3–6% of the mouse genome.
source: In both mouse lines, hundreds of genes were differentially expressed, comprising 3–6% of the mouse genome (Figure 6B; Figure 6—figure supplement 1), consistent with the magnitude of changes observed in other cell types and the high incidence of UG repeats recognized by TDP-43 in the genome (Humphrey et al., 2017).
evidence: This observation is supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1, and a citation to previous research.

claim: The differential gene expression profiles and gene ontology analysis were distinct between Mobp-TDP43 KO and Mog-TDP43 KO mouse lines.
source: The differential gene expression profiles and gene ontology analysis were also distinct between the mutant mouse lines (Figure 6B; Figure 6—figure supplement 2), with early deletion resulting in changes in mRNA processing and cell localization, and latter deletion resulting in changes in regulation of gene expression and metabolic processes.
evidence: This observation is supported by RNA-Seq data and gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Early deletion of TDP-43 resulted in changes in mRNA processing and cell localization.
source: The differential gene expression profiles and gene ontology analysis were also distinct between the mutant mouse lines (Figure 6B; Figure 6—figure supplement 2), with early deletion resulting in changes in mRNA processing and cell localization, and latter deletion resulting in changes in regulation of gene expression and metabolic processes.
evidence: This observation is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Late deletion of TDP-43 resulted in changes in regulation of gene expression and metabolic processes.
source: The differential gene expression profiles and gene ontology analysis were also distinct between the mutant mouse lines (Figure 6B; Figure 6—figure supplement 2), with early deletion resulting in changes in mRNA processing and cell localization, and latter deletion resulting in changes in regulation of gene expression and metabolic processes.
evidence: This observation is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Cryptic exons were often incorporated in mRNAs of the top 1% of the highest expressed genes enriched in oligodendrocytes.
source: Analysis of the top 1% of the highest expressed genes enriched in oligodendrocytes, many of which are involved in oligodendrocyte development and myelination, revealed that cryptic exons were often incorporated in their mRNAs (Figure 6F).
evidence: This observation is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis shown in Figure 6F.

claim: TDP-43 loss resulted in the emergence of a novel cryptic exon in intron 2 of the Ermn transcript.
source: These included Ermn (Ermin), an oligodendrocyte-specific cytoskeletal protein that regulates process branching and sheath extension (Brockschnieder et al., 2006). TDP-43 loss resulted in the emergence of a novel cryptic exon in intron 2 of the Ermn transcript (Figure 6C).
evidence: This observation is supported by RNA-Seq data shown in Figure 6C and a citation to previous research on Ermin function.

claim: RT-PCR validation using whole mouse brain indicated that aberrant splicing of Ermn generated novel splice isoforms, arising from cryptic exon incorporation, exon extension, and truncation.
source: RT-PCR validation using whole mouse brain indicated that this aberrant splicing generated novel splice isoforms, arising from cryptic exon incorporation, exon extension, and truncation (Figure 6D) that may lead to both gain and loss of function.
evidence: This observation is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Total Ermin protein was significantly lower in Mobp-TDP43-RCE KO brains compared to controls.
source: Total Ermin protein was significantly lower in Mobp-TDP43-RCE KO brains compared to controls (Figure 6E), and immunohistochemical staining revealed that Ermin was no longer detected in oligodendrocyte somata in these animals (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This observation is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 6E and immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: Ermin was no longer detected in oligodendrocyte somata in Mobp-TDP43-RCE KO animals.
source: Total Ermin protein was significantly lower in Mobp-TDP43-RCE KO brains compared to controls (Figure 6E), and immunohistochemical staining revealed that Ermin was no longer detected in oligodendrocyte somata in these animals (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This observation is supported by immunohistochemistry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3.

claim: OPCs represent the largest population of actively dividing cells in the brain outside the subventricular and subgranular germinal zones.
source: OPCs represent the largest population of actively dividing cells in the brain outside the subventricular and subgranular germinal zones (Dawson et al., 2003), and maintain a constant density through homeostatic proliferation, in which neighboring cells are induced to divide to replace cells lost through death or differentiation (Hughes et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: OPCs maintain a constant density through homeostatic proliferation, in which neighboring cells are induced to divide to replace cells lost through death or differentiation.
source: OPCs represent the largest population of actively dividing cells in the brain outside the subventricular and subgranular germinal zones (Dawson et al., 2003), and maintain a constant density through homeostatic proliferation, in which neighboring cells are induced to divide to replace cells lost through death or differentiation (Hughes et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Proliferative cells in many tissues are particularly vulnerable to perturbations in RNA processing, as they undergo metabolic reprogramming requiring extensive transcriptional reorganization.
source: Proliferative cells in many tissues are particularly vulnerable to perturbations in RNA processing, as they undergo metabolic reprogramming requiring extensive transcriptional reorganization (Petasny et al., 2021).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The higher basal rate of OPC proliferation in white matter reflects their higher rate of differentiation.
source: The higher basal rate of OPC proliferation in white matter, reflecting their higher rate of differentiation (Baracskay et al., 2002; Viganò et al., 2013), may be responsible for more rapid loss of OPCs in this region.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: All OPCs after 30 days of recovery were EGFP negative, indicating that they did not experience Cre activity.
source: Because Tardbp was not inactivated in all OPCs (the proportion limited by the efficiency of tamoxifen-induced recombination), surviving cells that retain TDP-43 are expected to proliferate to reconstitute the population. Consistent with this hypothesis, all OPCs after 30 days of recovery were EGFP negative (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D), indicating that they did not experience Cre activity.
evidence: This observation is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: OPCs have been shown to be exceptionally resistant to perturbations in their distribution and density.
source: Indeed, OPCs have been shown to be exceptionally resistant to perturbations in their distribution and density (Xing et al., 2021; Dang et al., 2019), and rapidly restore their numbers after mass differentiation following demyelination in mice (Baxi et al., 2017; Penderis et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: OPCs rapidly restore their numbers after mass differentiation following demyelination in mice.
source: Indeed, OPCs have been shown to be exceptionally resistant to perturbations in their distribution and density (Xing et al., 2021; Dang et al., 2019), and rapidly restore their numbers after mass differentiation following demyelination in mice (Baxi et al., 2017; Penderis et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Reductions in OPC density have been observed in some human MS lesions.
source: Nevertheless, reductions in OPC density have been observed in some human MS lesions (Chang et al., 2000), suggesting that other environmental changes, such as persistent inflammation or gliosis, which may induce TDP-43 mislocalization, may impede their homeostasis and impair their ability to detect demyelinated axons and generate new oligodendrocytes.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The half-life of TDP-43 in vitro was measured to be 12–34 hr.
source: As the half-life of TDP-43 in vitro was measured to be 12–34 hr (Ling et al., 2010; Lee et al., 2011), it is possible that sufficient residual TDP-43 RNA/protein remains from the OPC stage to enable these initial transitions.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Subtler manipulations of mature oligodendrocytes, such as reduction in expression of Kir4.1 or deletion of MCT1, is sufficient to alter neuronal excitability.
source: Previous studies have shown that subtler manipulations of mature oligodendrocytes, such as reduction in expression of the inwardly rectifying potassium channel Kir4.1 (Larson et al., 2018) or deletion of the lactate transporter MCT1 (Philips et al., 2021), is sufficient to alter neuronal excitability, highlighting possible functional consequences of TDP-43 loss from these myelinating cells.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Abnormal myelination and altered density of oligodendrocytes have been correlated with neural hyperexcitability and circuit dysfunction in neurodevelopmental disorders such as autism spectrum disorders and schizophrenia.
source: In neurodevelopmental disorders, such as autism spectrum disorders and schizophrenia, abnormal myelination and altered density of oligodendrocytes have been correlated with neural hyperexcitability and circuit dysfunction (Phan et al., 2020; Fields, 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Oligodendrocyte turnover and demyelination in the adult CNS have been shown to be accompanied by inflammation and neuronal death in neurodegenerative diseases such as ALS and AD.
source: In contrast, oligodendrocyte turnover and demyelination in the adult CNS have been shown to be accompanied by inflammation and neuronal death in neurodegenerative diseases, such as ALS and AD (Kang et al., 2013; Desai et al., 2010; Behrendt et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Oligodendrocytes in vitro have an intrinsic ability to wrap structures of appropriate caliber (>0.4 µm), including inert nanofibers and fixed axons.
source: In vitro studies indicate that oligodendrocytes have an intrinsic ability to wrap structures of appropriate caliber (>0.4 µm), including inert nanofibers and fixed axons (Rosenberg et al., 2008; Mei et al., 2013; Lee et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Inappropriate myelination of neuronal somata has been observed after deletion of adhesive proteins (e.g., JAM2) from neurons.
source: Inappropriate myelination of neuronal somata has been observed after deletion of adhesive proteins (e.g., JAM2) from neurons (Redmond et al., 2016), expression of a mutant form of a cell adhesion protein (e.g., Cadm4) in oligodendrocytes (Elazar et al., 2019), or overexpression of MBP (Almeida et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Similar aberrant myelination has been recently described in MS lesions.
source: Similar aberrant myelination has been recently described in MS lesions (Neely et al., 2022), where TDP-43 mislocalization has also be observed (Masaki et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: TDP-43 mislocalization has been observed in MS lesions.
source: Similar aberrant myelination has been recently described in MS lesions (Neely et al., 2022), where TDP-43 mislocalization has also be observed (Masaki et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: TDP-43 maintains the integrity of the cellular transcriptome by regulating splicing of pre-mRNAs and suppressing incorporation of cryptic exons.
source: TDP-43 maintains the integrity of the cellular transcriptome by regulating splicing of pre-mRNAs and suppressing incorporation of cryptic exons. By efficiently binding to UG microsatellite repeats within intronic sequences, TDP-43 ensures that spliceosomes skip over these regions during normal splicing (Ling et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: TDP-43-dependent cryptic exons are both cell type and species specific.
source: As the specificity of TDP-43 targets primarily depend on the location of these UG tandem repeats, TDP-43-dependent cryptic exons are both cell type and species specific (Jeong et al., 2017; Ling et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Nfasc, which is misspliced in TDP-43-deficient Schwann cells, was not alternatively spliced in TDP-43-null oligodendrocytes.
source: Nfasc, which is misspliced in TDP-43-deficient Schwann cells (Chang et al., 2021), was not alternatively spliced in TDP-43-null oligodendrocytes, further confirming the cell-type-specific actions of TDP-43.
evidence: This observation is supported by RNA-Seq data analysis and a citation to previous research.

claim: Oligodendrocyte and myelin abnormalities have been reported in many neurodegenerative diseases known to present with TDP-43 proteinopathy.
source: Oligodendrocyte and myelin abnormalities have been reported in many neurodegenerative diseases known to present with TDP-43 proteinopathy (Kang et al., 2013; Masaki et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Nuclear clearance of TDP-43 and resulting loss of function is sufficient to cause dramatic alterations in pre-mRNA splicing.
source: Although cytoplasmic aggregates of TDP-43 are not always present, nuclear clearance of TDP-43 and resulting loss of function is sufficient to cause dramatic alterations in pre-mRNA splicing (Sun et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Loss of TDP-43 function in oligodendrocytes may contribute to neuronal dysfunction in neurodegenerative disease.
source: Inducible deletion of TDP-43 from oligodendrocytes in the adult central nervous system (CNS) induced the same progressive morphological changes and mice acquired profound hindlimb weakness, suggesting that loss of TDP-43 function in oligodendrocytes may contribute to neuronal dysfunction in neurodegenerative disease.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results showing motor deficits after adult-onset TDP-43 deletion.

claim: Aberrant splicing of Ermin mRNA is predicted to lead to a truncated N-terminal peptide (~amino acid 1–110) that may produce a dominant negative effect.
source: In case of Ermin, a cytoskeletal protein involved in oligodendrocyte morphogenesis (Brockschnieder et al., 2006), cryptic exon incorporation led to a pronounced decrease in protein expression; however, the phenotypic changes induced by loss of TDP-43 are not the same as that observed in Ermn KO mice (Wang et al., 2020; Ziaei et al., 2020). Aberrant splicing of Ermin mRNA is predicted to lead to a truncated N-terminal peptide (~amino acid 1–110) that may produce a dominant negative effect.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the observed splicing changes and comparison to Ermn KO phenotypes.
